title: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
summary: Understand the three core browser languages, the boundary each owns, and how they cooperate without becoming tangled.
prerequisites: How the Web Works is helpful but not required.
learningOutcomes: Assign structure, presentation, and behavior to the correct language.
Explain the DOM, cascade, and event-driven behavior.
Build a progressively enhanced, accessible component.

heroVisual.title: One interface, three responsibilities
heroVisual.caption: The layers cooperate best when each retains a clear job.

nodes.label: HTML
nodes.detail: Defines meaning, order, relationships, and native controls.

nodes.label: CSS
nodes.detail: Controls layout, typography, color, states, and adaptation.

nodes.label: JavaScript
nodes.detail: Responds to events, coordinates state, and changes behavior.

nodes.label: Browser APIs
nodes.detail: Expose the document, network, storage, media, and device capabilities.

sections.title: 1. HTML creates the meaningful document
sections.summary: HTML should describe what content is before describing how it looks.

blocks.text: HTML provides the document outline, landmarks, controls, labels, links, media alternatives, and relationships that browsers and assistive technologies can understand before CSS or JavaScript runs.

blocks.explanation: The elements communicate that this is a self-contained article with a heading, paragraph, and real destination.

items.title: Use native elements
items.summary: Buttons, links, inputs, details, tables, and headings already carry behavior and semantics.
items.whenToUse: Start with the element whose built-in meaning matches the task.
items.avoidWhen: Avoid replacing a button with a clickable div.

items.title: Keep heading order meaningful
items.whenToUse: Use levels to represent sections, not visual size.
items.avoidWhen: Do not skip levels only to get a preferred appearance.

items.title: Name controls
items.summary: Every input needs a programmatic name.
items.whenToUse: Use a visible label whenever possible.
items.avoidWhen: Placeholder text is not a replacement for a label.

blocks.title: Semantic HTML
blocks.body: Markup whose element choices communicate the role and structure of the content, not merely its appearance.

sections.title: 2. CSS computes presentation from rules
sections.summary: The cascade resolves competing declarations; layout then responds to content and context.

visual.title: From selector to pixels
visual.caption: A declaration is only one input to the computed result.

nodes.label: Cascade
nodes.detail: Origin, importance, layer, specificity, scope, and order resolve conflicts.

nodes.label: Compute
nodes.detail: Relative values and inherited properties become usable values.

nodes.label: Layout
nodes.detail: Formatting contexts size and place boxes.

nodes.label: Paint
nodes.detail: Color, borders, text, effects, and layers are drawn.

items: Prefer intrinsic sizing, wrapping, minmax(), and auto-fit before breakpoints.

sections.title: 3. JavaScript coordinates behavior and state
sections.summary: JavaScript adds behavior; it should not recreate capabilities the platform already provides.

blocks.text: JavaScript runs tasks, reacts to events, calls browser APIs, updates state, and can change the DOM. Because it can delay interaction or fail entirely, essential content and navigation should not depend on unnecessary scripting.

blocks.explanation: The event changes one explicit state and keeps the exposed accessibility state synchronized.

items.title: Events
items.summary: Signals such as click, input, submit, and keydown.
items.whenToUse: Use event delegation when many similar descendants behave alike.

items.title: State
items.summary: The minimum data needed to derive the current interface.
items.whenToUse: Keep one owner for each state value.

items.title: Effects
items.summary: Work outside pure calculation, such as network requests or storage.

blocks.title: More JavaScript is not automatically more capability
blocks.body: Native HTML and CSS often provide faster, more resilient, and more accessible behavior with no runtime bundle cost.

sections.title: 4. The layers cooperate through stable boundaries
sections.summary: A component is easier to change when meaning, appearance, and behavior are not fused.

items.title: Start with the task
items.explanation: Describe what the person must understand or do.
items.result: The requirement is independent of technology.

items.title: Choose semantic HTML
items.explanation: Create a usable reading and interaction order.
items.result: The component works with basic browser behavior.

items.title: Add adaptive CSS
items.explanation: Make the component legible in every available container.

items.title: Add only necessary JavaScript
items.explanation: Introduce state or orchestration that native behavior cannot provide.

items.title: Verify every layer
items.explanation: Test keyboard, pointer, touch, zoom, reduced motion, and failure states.

blocks.title: Progressive enhancement
blocks.body: Begin with a functional baseline, then add capabilities when the browser supports them. This is a reliability strategy, not a preference for plain design.

items: A link navigates; a button performs an action.
Visual order and reading order remain aligned.
State is represented in the DOM when users need to perceive it.
Loading and error states are part of the component contract.

sections.title: 5. Responsive means content survives changing context
sections.summary: A responsive interface changes priorities and composition, not merely scale.

rows: Preserve primary content and actions in one clear sequence.
Identity, title, current task, primary action.
Reveal comparisons and local navigation when they reduce backtracking.
Add parallel orientation without lengthening prose indefinitely.
Bounded reading measure and contextual rail.
Reflow rather than clip, overlap, or truncate meaning.
blocks.caption: Adaptation decisions follow task priority

blocks.title: Breakpoints are evidence of content pressure
blocks.body: Add a breakpoint where the current composition stops working, not at a device brand or model width.

items: No page-level horizontal scrolling at 320 CSS pixels.
Interactive targets meet the required target-size outcome or spacing exception.
The design works in both orientations.
Motion and color do not carry the only meaning.
